clauses.text: These Directions shall be called the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks Fraud Risk Management) Directions, 2026.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: A. Short Title and Commencement

clauses.text: These Directions shall come into effect immediately upon issuance.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: A. Short Title and Commencement

clauses.text: These Directions shall be applicable to Commercial Banks (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'banks' and individually as 'bank').
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: B. Applicability

clauses.text: For the purpose of these Directions , 'Commercial Banks' is the term applied to banking  companies  (other  than  Small  Finance  Banks,  Payments  Banks,  and Local Area Banks), corresponding new banks, and the State Bank of India, as defined respectively under clauses (c), (da), and (nc) of Section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: B. Applicability

clauses.text: In these Directions, unless the context states otherwise, the terms herein shall bear the meaning assigned to them below:
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Central Fraud Registry (CFR)' is a web-based searchable database maintained by RBI.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'CRILC' is the Central Repository of Information on Large Credits as referred to in the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Supervisory Returns) Directions, 2026.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: Date of classification', for the purpose of reporting under FMR, is the date when due approval from the competent authority has been obtained for such classification, and the reasoned order is passed.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: Date of detection to be reported in FMR, is the actual date when the fraud came to light in the concerned branch / audit / department of the bank, as the case may be, and not the date of approval by the competent authority of the bank.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: Date of occurrence , for the purpose of reporting under FMR, is the date when the actual misappropriation of funds has started taking place, or the event occurred, as evidenced / reported in the audit or other findings.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: 'Red Flagged Account' is one where suspicion of fraudulent activity is thrown up by the presence of one or more Early Warning Signal (EWS) indicators, alerting / triggering deeper investigation from potential fraud angle and requiring initiation of preventive measures by all banks.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: C. Definitions

clauses.text: The bank shall put in place a Board approved Policy on Fraud Risk Management delineating roles and responsibilities of Board / Board Committees and Senior Management of the bank.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: In this context , 'Board' will refer to 'Board of Directors' in case of a domestic bank, and 'Local Advisory Board' in case of a Foreign Bank operating in India.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The Policy shall also incorporate measures for ensuring compliance with principles of natural justice in a time-bound manner, which at a minimum, shall include:
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: Issuance of a detailed Show Cause Notice (SCN) to the Persons (including Third Party Service Providers and Professionals, inter-alia, architects, valuers, chartered accountants, advocates and other professionals/service providers), Entities and their Promoters/Whole-time and Executive Directors against whom allegation of fraud is being examined.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The SCN shall provide complete details of transactions/actions/events basis which declaration and reporting of a fraud is being contemplated under these Directions.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: As non-whole-time directors (like nominee directors and independent directors) are normally not in charge of, or responsible to the company for the conduct of business of the company, the bank may take this into consideration before proceeding against such directors under these Directions.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: 1 Refer to the judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court dated March 27, 2023 on Civil Appeal No.7300 of 2022 in the matter of State Bank of India & Ors Vs. Rajesh Agarwal & Ors. and connected matters, read with the Order dated May 12, 2023 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Misc. Application. No.810 of 2023, specifically in relation to serving a notice, giving an opportunity to submit a representation before classifying Persons/Entities as fraud and passing a reasoned order.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The bank shall provide a reasonable time of not less than 21 days to the Persons/Entities on whom the SCN was served to respond to the said SCN.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The bank shall have a well laid out system for issuance of SCN and examination of the responses/submissions made by the Persons/Entities prior to declaring such Persons/Entities as fraudulent.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The bank shall serve a reasoned Order on the Persons/Entities conveying its decision regarding declaration/classification of the account as fraud or otherwise.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The Board shall review the Fraud Risk Management Policy at least once in three years, or more frequently, as may be prescribed by the Board.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: Special Committee of the Board for Monitoring and Follow-up of cases of Frauds:
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The bank shall constitute a Committee of the Board to be known as 'Special Committee of the Board for Monitoring and Follow-up of cases of Frauds' (SCBMF) with a minimum of three members of the Board, consisting of a whole-time director and a minimum of two independent directors/non-executive directors.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The Committee shall oversee the effectiveness of the Fraud Risk Management in the bank.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The SCBMF shall review and monitor cases of frauds, including root cause analysis, and suggest mitigating measures for strengthening the internal controls, risk management framework and minimising the incidence of frauds.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The Board of the bank shall decide the coverage and periodicity of such reviews.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The coverage may include, among others, categories/trends of frauds, industry/sectoral/geographical concentration of frauds, delay in detection/classification of frauds and delay in examination/conclusion of staff accountability.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The Senior Management shall be responsible for implementation of the fraud risk management policy approved by the Board of the bank.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The Senior Management of the bank shall also place a periodic review of incidents of fraud before Board/Audit Committee of Board (ACB), as appropriate.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The bank shall put in place a transparent mechanism to ensure that Whistle Blower complaints on possible fraud cases/suspicious activities in account(s) are examined and concluded appropriately under its Whistle Blower Policy.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The bank shall set-up an appropriate organisational structure for institutionalisation of Fraud Risk Management within its overall risk management functions/departments.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.text: The bank shall have a framework for EWS and Red Flagging of Accounts (RFA) under the overall Fraud Risk Management Policy approved by the Board.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: A. Governance Structure

clauses.text: The RMCB shall oversee the effectiveness of the Board-approved framework for EWS and RFA.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: A. Governance Structure

clauses.text: The Senior Management shall be responsible for implementation of a robust Framework for EWS and RFA within the bank.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: A. Governance Structure

clauses.text: The RMCB shall approve the EWS indicators identified for monitoring credit facilities / loan accounts and other banking transactions.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: A. Governance Structure

clauses.text: The RMCB shall prescribe appropriate Turnaround Time (TAT), preferably not more than 30 days, for examination of EWS alerts / triggers.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: A. Governance Structure

clauses.text: RMC shall review the status of red flagged accounts, including the EWS alerts / triggers and remedial actions initiated by the bank at periodic intervals as approved by the Board.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: A. Governance Structure

clauses.text: The EWS / RFA framework shall be subject to suitable validation in accordance with the directions of RMCB so as to ensure its integrity, robustness and consistency of the outcomes.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: A. Governance Structure

clauses.text: The EWS / RFA Framework shall provide for, among others: A system of robust EWS which is integrated with Core Banking Solution (CBS) or other operational systems; Initiation of remedial action on alerts / triggers from EWS System in a timely manner; Periodic review of credit sanction and monitoring processes, internal controls and systems; and Effective use of CRILC database and the CFR.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: A. Governance Structure

clauses.text: The bank shall put in place / suitably upgrade its existing EWS system on an ongoing basis.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: A. Governance Structure

clauses.text: Development of EWS System : The EWS system shall be comprehensive and designed to include both the quantitative and qualitative indicators to make the framework robust and effective.
clauses.reason: shall
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: B. EWS / RFA Framework for Credit Facilities / Loan Accounts

clauses.text: Data Analytics and Market Intelligence (MI) Unit: The bank shall set up a dedicated Data Analytics and MI Unit keeping in view its size, complexity, business mix and risk profile.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: B. EWS / RFA Framework for Credit Facilities / Loan Accounts

clauses.text: Generation of EWS alert(s) / trigger(s) shall necessitate examination whether the account needs to be red flagged and consequently, investigation from potential fraud angle.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: B. EWS / RFA Framework for Credit Facilities / Loan Accounts

clauses.text: The bank shall report a n account, with an aggregate exposure of ₹3 crore and above, once red flagged in 'Red Flagged Account Return' on the Reserve Bank's CRILC platform within seven days of being red flagged.
clauses.reason: must
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: B. EWS / RFA Framework for Credit Facilities / Loan Accounts

clauses.text: 'Exposure' in this context, shall include all fund-based and non-fund-based exposures.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: B. EWS / RFA Framework for Credit Facilities / Loan Accounts

clauses.text: The bank shall develop / strengthen its EWS system by identifying suitable indicators and parameterising them in its EWS system for monitoring other banking / non-credit related transactions.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: C. EWS Framework for Other Banking / Non-Credit Related Transactions

clauses.text: The bank shall strive to continuously upgrade the EWS system for enhancing its integrity and robustness, monitor other banking / non-credit related transactions efficiently and prevent fraudulent activities through the banking channel.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: C. EWS Framework for Other Banking / Non-Credit Related Transactions

clauses.text: Further, the effectiveness of EWS system shall be tested periodically.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: C. EWS Framework for Other Banking / Non-Credit Related Transactions

clauses.text: The design and specification of EWS system shall be robust and resilient to ensure that integrity of system is maintained, personal and financial data of customers are secure and transaction monitoring for prevention/detection of potential fraud is on real-time basis or with minimum time lag without compromising the effectiveness of the outcome of EWS system in prevention/detection of potential frauds.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: C. EWS Framework for Other Banking / Non-Credit Related Transactions

clauses.text: The bank shall remain vigilant in monitoring transactions/unusual activities, specifically in the non-KYC compliant and money mule accounts, to contain unauthorised/fraudulent transactions and to prevent misuse of banking channel.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline, monetary penalty, mandatory disclosure obligation, or explicit compliance requirement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: C. EWS Framework for Other Banking / Non-Credit Related Transactions

clauses.text: The Data Analytics and MI Unit or other dedicated analytics set up in the bank shall extensively monitor and analyse other banking/non-credit related transactions, more specifically the transactions through digital platforms and applications, in order to identify unusual patterns and activities which could alert the bank timely in initiating appropriate measures towards prevention of fraudulent activities.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: C. EWS Framework for Other Banking / Non-Credit Related Transactions

clauses.text: The bank shall use an external audit, or an internal audit as per its Board approved Policy, for further investigation in such accounts.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: A. Credit  facility  /  Loan  account  classified  as  Red-flagged  Account  and Reporting of Fraud

clauses.text: The bank shall frame a policy on engagement of external auditors covering aspects such as due diligence, competency and track record of the auditors, among others.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: A. Credit  facility  /  Loan  account  classified  as  Red-flagged  Account  and Reporting of Fraud

clauses.text: Further, the contractual agreement with the auditors shall, inter alia, contain suitable clauses on timeline for completion of the audit and submission of audit report to the bank within a specified time limit, as approved by the Board.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: A. Credit  facility  /  Loan  account  classified  as  Red-flagged  Account  and Reporting of Fraud

clauses.text: The loan agreement with the borrower shall contain clauses for conduct of such audit at the behest of lender(s) consequent upon red flagging of the account.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: A. Credit  facility  /  Loan  account  classified  as  Red-flagged  Account  and Reporting of Fraud

clauses.text: In cases where the audit report submitted remains inconclusive or is delayed due to non-cooperation by the borrower, the bank shall conclude on status of the account as a fraud or otherwise based on the material available on its record and its own internal investigation / assessment in such cases.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: A. Credit  facility  /  Loan  account  classified  as  Red-flagged  Account  and Reporting of Fraud

clauses.text: The bank shall ensure that principles of natural justice are strictly adhered to before classifying / declaring an account as fraud (refer to Paragraph 6).
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: A. Credit  facility  /  Loan  account  classified  as  Red-flagged  Account  and Reporting of Fraud

clauses.text: The decision to classify any account, either standard or NPA, as a red-flagged account shall be at the individual bank level and such bank(s) shall report the status of the account on Reserve Bank's CRILC platform immediately (not later than seven days from date of classification as a red-flagged account).
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: A. Credit  facility  /  Loan  account  classified  as  Red-flagged  Account  and Reporting of Fraud

clauses.text: The bank (in case of sole lending) or the individual banks (in case of multiple banking arrangement or consortium lending) shall ensure that the principles of natural justice (refer Paragraph 6) are strictly adhered to before classifying / declaring an account as fraud.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: A. Credit  facility  /  Loan  account  classified  as  Red-flagged  Account  and Reporting of Fraud

clauses.text: Once an account has been red-flagged, the entire process of classification of the account as fraud or removal of red-flagged status shall ordinarily be completed within 180 days from the date of first reporting of the account as red-flagged on CRILC platform.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: A. Credit  facility  /  Loan  account  classified  as  Red-flagged  Account  and Reporting of Fraud

clauses.text: Cases remaining in red-flagged status beyond 180 days shall be reported to the SCBMF for review with adequate reasoning / justification thereof. Such cases shall also be subject to supervisory review by RBI.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: A. Credit  facility  /  Loan  account  classified  as  Red-flagged  Account  and Reporting of Fraud

clauses.text: In case an account is identified as a fraud by any bank, the borrowal accounts of other group companies, in which one or more promoter(s) / whole-time director(s) are common, shall also be subjected to examination by Regulated Entities (REs) concerned from fraud angle under these Directions.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: A. Credit  facility  /  Loan  account  classified  as  Red-flagged  Account  and Reporting of Fraud

clauses.text: In cases where Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs) have suo moto initiated investigation involving a borrower account, the bank shall immediately red-flag the account and follow the usual process for classification of account as fraud and complete the same within the stipulated period as specified at Paragraph 31 above.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: A. Credit  facility  /  Loan  account  classified  as  Red-flagged  Account  and Reporting of Fraud

clauses.text: The bank shall, after complying with the principles of natural justice, report to Indian Banks' Association (IBA) the details of such third parties or professionals involved in frauds.
clauses.reason: report to IBA
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: B. Independent  Confirmation  from  Third-party  Service  Providers  including Professionals

clauses.text: The bank shall initiate and complete the examination of staff accountability in all fraud cases in a time-bound manner in accordance with its internal policy.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: C. Staff Accountability

clauses.text: Refer to Large Exposure Framework in the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Concentration Risk Management) Directions, 2025
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: C. Staff Accountability

clauses.text: Public Sector Banks (PSBs) shall conduct examination of staff accountability as per the guidelines issued by the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC).
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: C. Staff Accountability

clauses.text: In terms of CVC Orders, PSBs shall also refer all fraud cases of amount involving ₹3 crore and above for examining the role of all levels of officials / whole-time directors (including ex-officials / ex-WTDs) to the Advisory Board for Banking and Financial Frauds (ABBFF).
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: C. Staff Accountability

clauses.text: In cases involving very senior executives of the bank (MD & CEO / Executive Director / Executives of equivalent rank), the ACB shall initiate examination of their accountability and place it before the Board.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: C. Staff Accountability

clauses.text: Such executives shall not participate in the meeting of the Board / ACB / SCBMF in which their accountability is to be considered.
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard requirement
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: C. Staff Accountability

clauses.text: However, in case of PSBs, such cases shall also be referred to the ABBFF.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: C. Staff Accountability

clauses.text: Persons / Entities classified and reported as fraud by the bank and also Entities and Persons associated with such Entities,  shall  be  debarred  from  raising  of funds and / or seeking additional credit facilities from financial entities regulated by RBI, for a period of five years from the date of full repayment of the defrauded amount / settlement amount agreed upon in case of a compromise settlement.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: D. Penal Measures

clauses.text: the lending bank shall have the sole discretion to entertain or decline such requests for credit facilities after the expiry of the mandatory cooling period
clauses.reason: mandatory cooling period
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: Explanation :

clauses.text: falls within the definition of a 'joint venture' or an 'associate company'
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: Explanation :

clauses.text: is deemed to be associated with it
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: Explanation :

clauses.text: as updated from time to time
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: Explanation :

clauses.text: as updated from time to time
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: Explanation :

clauses.text: In case an entity classified as fraud has subsequently undergone a resolution either under Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) or under the resolution framework of RBI 4 , resulting in a change in the management and control of the entity  /  business  enterprise,  the  bank  shall  examine  whether  the  entity  shall continue  to  remain  classified  as  fraud  or  the  classification  as  fraud  could  be removed after  implementation  of  the  Resolution  Plan  under  IBC  or  aforesaid resolution framework.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: E. Treatment of Accounts under Resolution

clauses.text: The penal measures as detailed in Paragraphs 39 and 40 shall not be applicable to  entities  /  business  enterprises  after  implementation  of  the  Resolution  Plan under IBC or aforesaid resolution framework.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: E. Treatment of Accounts under Resolution

clauses.text: The penal measures detailed in Paragraphs 39 and 40 shall continue to apply to the  erstwhile  promoter(s)  /  director(s)  /  persons  who  were  in  charge  and responsible for the management of the affairs of the entity / business enterprise.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IV - General Instructions :: E. Treatment of Accounts under Resolution

clauses.text: The bank shall immediately report the incidents of fraud to LEAs, subject to applicable laws, as indicated below
clauses.reason: clause imposes a hard deadline
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter V - Reporting of Frauds to Law Enforcement Agencies :: Note:

clauses.text: In case of consortium lending, each of the consortium member may file separate complaints, if separate offences have been committed in respect of each of them and if the fraud so committed is not part of the same fraudulent act/transaction
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter V - Reporting of Frauds to Law Enforcement Agencies :: Note:

clauses.text: The bank is, however, advised to mandatorily report incidents of fraud involving an amount of ₹1 lakh or more to LEAs
clauses.reason: clause imposes a mandatory disclosure obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter V - Reporting of Frauds to Law Enforcement Agencies :: Note:

clauses.text: The bank shall establish suitable nodal point(s) / designate officer(s) for reporting incidents of fraud to LEAs and for proper coordination to meet the requirements of the LEAs
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter V - Reporting of Frauds to Law Enforcement Agencies :: Note:

clauses.text: To ensure uniformity and consistency while reporting incidents of fraud to RBI through Fraud Monitoring Returns (FMRs) using online portal, the bank shall choose the most appropriate category from any one of the following:
clauses.reason: shall
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Misappropriation of funds and criminal breach of trust;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Fraudulent encashment through forged instruments;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Manipulation of books of accounts or through fictitious accounts, and conversion of property;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Cheating by concealment of facts with the intention to deceive any person and cheating by impersonation;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Forgery with the intention to commit fraud by making any false documents / electronic records;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Wilful falsification, destruction, alteration, mutilations of any book, electronic record, paper, writing, valuable security or account with intent to defraud;
clauses.reason: shall not
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Fraudulent credit facilities extended for illegal gratification;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Cash shortages on account of frauds;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Fraudulent transactions involving foreign exchange;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Fraudulent electronic banking / digital payment related transactions committed on banks;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Other type of fraudulent activity not covered under any of the above.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: The bank shall put in place systems and procedures to ensure that the information available in Central Fraud Registry (CFR) is used for credit risk and fraud risk management effectively.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: B. Central Fraud Registry

clauses.text: The bank is required to report payment system related disputed / suspected or attempted fraudulent transactions to Central Payments Fraud Information Registry (CPFIR), as required in terms of Circular Ref. CO.DPSS.OVRST. No.S1619/06-08-005/2022-23 dated December 26, 2022, maintained by RBI.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: B. Central Fraud Registry

clauses.text: The bank shall furnish FMR in individual fraud cases, irrespective of the amount involved, immediately, but not later than 14 days from the date of classification of an incident / account as fraud.
clauses.reason: imposes a hard deadline
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: C. Modalities of Reporting Incidents of Fraud
